Four lattes, four hometowns

Each signature is named for a Palestinian city and built on espresso and steamed milk. Pick one — every iced version is finished with cold foam.

    Come for the coffee. Stay for the community.

    Cafe Palestina opened in July 2026 in a low-key plaza on Alondra Blvd — follow the pathway of red, white and green lights to the door. Inside, keffiyeh-inspired details run through the room, and the menu reads like a map: Akka, Gaza, Al-Quds.

    It was built as a third space as much as a coffee shop — early enough for the 5 AM crowd, open late enough for midnight study sessions, and loud with regulars in between.

    • Opened July 2026 — Norwalk's Palestinian-inspired cafe, at 10929 Alondra Blvd.
    • More than a counter — L.A. Taco described it as “a statement, a room built to make a community feel like it belongs.”
    • 19 hours a day — 5 AM to midnight, every single day.

    Before you come

    What should I order first?

    Start with the Latte Milh Akka — the pistachio latte the cafe calls “The Favorite.” If you want warm spice instead, go Latte Gazawi with cinnamon and condensed milk.

    What are the hours?

    Every day, 5:00 AM to 12:00 AM — early-morning coffee runs and late-night sessions both covered.

    Where exactly is it?

    10929 Alondra Blvd, Norwalk, CA 90650, in the plaza on Alondra — look for the red, white and green lights leading to the door.

    Can I get it delivered?

    Yes — listed on DoorDash and Caviar for delivery.

    Where do new menu items show up?

    On Instagram first. Follow @cafepalestina.usa for the updated menu posts and new drops.
